verdict.rationale: PayPal's ACP/UCP flows use delegated, single-use payment tokens that are "bound to your merchant ID and include amount and time restrictions that you can configure" (paypal-ac-supp-acp-chatgpt, paypal-ac-supp-ucp-googlepay), which functions as a scoped, time-limited authorization rather than an open-ended charge, and the agent-toolkit docs advise "keep human oversight in areas where personal judgment matters most" (paypal-ac-supp-agent-toolkit). However, none of the docs describe an explicit signed mandate, a PayPal-hosted confirmation screen, or a documented per-purchase consent UX owned by PayPal — checkout confirmation appears to live inside ChatGPT's own Instant Checkout UI, not as a PayPal-documented approval artifact. Missing for 10: an explicit PayPal-side confirmation/consent UI, a signed-mandate object or receipt, and any evidence (docs or hands-on) that money cannot move without a captured user approval step.
